hints: Model the shaded minor segment as sector $AOC$ minus triangle $AOC$.
Use the angle in the semicircle to show that $\angle AOC=\pi-2\theta$.
Write the segment area as $\tfrac12r^2(\pi-2\theta)-\tfrac12r^2\sin(\pi-2\theta)$ and equate it to one third of the semicircle area.
Cancel $r^2$, use $\sin(\pi-2\theta)=\sin2\theta$, and rearrange until $\theta$ is isolated.
walkthrough:
Find angle $AOC$ in triangle $OAC$:
Since $OA = OC = r$, triangle $OAC$ is isosceles with base angles $\angle OAC = \angle OCA = \theta$.
The angle sum of triangle $OAC$ gives:
$$\angle AOC = \pi - (\theta + \theta) = \pi - 2\theta$$

Express the area of sector $AOC$:
$$\text{Area}(\text{sector } AOC) = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2(\angle AOC) = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2(\pi - 2\theta)$$

Express the area of triangle $AOC$ using $\sin(\pi - 2\theta) = \sin 2\theta$:
$$\text{Area}(\triangle AOC) = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2\sin(\pi - 2\theta) = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2\sin 2\theta$$

Subtract the area of the triangle from the area of the sector to obtain the area of the shaded segment:
$$\text{Area}(\text{segment}) = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2(\pi - 2\theta) - \dfrac{1}{2}r^2\sin 2\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2(\pi - 2\theta - \sin 2\theta)$$

Equate the segment area to one third of the area of the semicircle $\dfrac{1}{2}\pi r^2$:
$$\dfrac{1}{2}r^2(\pi - 2\theta - \sin 2\theta) = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\pi r^2\right) = \dfrac{1}{6}\pi r^2$$

hints: Bracket the fixed point by comparing $\theta$ with $g(\theta)=\tfrac13(\pi-1.5\sin2\theta)$ at both endpoints.
Calculate $g(0.5)$ and $g(0.7)$ in radians, keeping at least 2 significant figures.
Show explicitly that $g(0.5)-0.5$ and $g(0.7)-0.7$ have opposite signs, which places a solution between the endpoints.
walkthrough: Define the fixed-point function $g(\theta) = \dfrac{1}{3}(\pi - 1.5\sin 2\theta)$ and the residual function $f(\theta) = g(\theta) - \theta$.
Conclude that because $f(\theta)$ is continuous on $[0.5, 0.7]$ and exhibits a sign change ($f(0.5) > 0$ and $f(0.7) < 0$), the root $\theta$ satisfies $0.5 < \theta < 0.7$.

hints: Use the equation from part (a) as the fixed-point iteration $\theta_{n+1}=\tfrac13(\pi-1.5\sin2\theta_n)$.
Choose a starting value in the bracket from part (b), work in radians, and feed each calculated value back into the formula.
Record every iterate to 5 decimal places until successive values settle sufficiently to justify a unique rounding to 3 decimal places.
walkthrough:
Set up the iterative formula based on part (a):
$$\theta_{n+1} = \dfrac{1}{3}(\pi - 1.5\sin 2\theta_n)$$

Choose a starting value $\theta_0 = 0.6$ within $[0.5, 0.7]$ and evaluate successive iterates in radians to 5 decimal places:
$$\theta_1 = \dfrac{1}{3}(\pi - 1.5\sin(2 \times 0.6)) \approx 0.58118$$
$$\theta_2 = \dfrac{1}{3}(\pi - 1.5\sin(2 \times 0.58118)) \approx 0.58833$$
$$\theta_3 = \dfrac{1}{3}(\pi - 1.5\sin(2 \times 0.58833)) \approx 0.58553$$
$$\theta_4 = \dfrac{1}{3}(\pi - 1.5\sin(2 \times 0.58553)) \approx 0.58661$$
$$\theta_5 = \dfrac{1}{3}(\pi - 1.5\sin(2 \times 0.58661)) \approx 0.58619$$
$$\theta_6 = \dfrac{1}{3}(\pi - 1.5\sin(2 \times 0.58619)) \approx 0.58636$$

Confirm the rounding to 3 decimal places by evaluating $f(\theta) = g(\theta) - \theta$ at the rounding boundaries $0.5855$ and $0.5865$:
$$f(0.5855) \approx 0.58662 - 0.5855 = +0.00112 > 0$$
$$f(0.5865) \approx 0.58624 - 0.5865 = -0.00026 < 0$$

Since there is a sign change across $(0.5855, 0.5865)$, conclude that $\theta$ correct to 3 decimal places is:
$$\theta = 0.586$$
